: O R D E R :
MR.
P.K.CHATTOPADHYAY, LD. MEMBER 

 

 This Appeal arose out of judgement and order dt.
29.10.09 in DCDRF, Kolkata Unit-I Case No. 115/2008 where the Complainant, Mr.
Santosh Kr. Kanodia, purchased one Microwave Oven on 23.12.06 at a cost of Rs.
8,300/- from the OP No. 1, namely Great Eastern Appliances Pvt. Ltd.,
manufactured by OP No. 2 namely Videocon Industries Ltd. The given oven malfunctioned after some
domestic use in March, 2007 when it was repaired but stopped functioning
altogether again in August, 2007, when after much prodding and many efforts,
the oven was found to have dead PCB, but relevant PCB could not be found. The oven was finally replaced through a new
one around 23.10.07 which again failed to work in February, 2008 and thereafter
no action in rectification followed in spite of many initiatives. Thus, the complaint case seeking refund of
the purchase amount of Rs. 8,300/- on return of the junk oven with compensation
of Rs. 1.00 lakhs with further orders as deemed fit.
The Ops contested the case when OP No. 1 & OP No. 2 in
their written version stated inter alia that there was no deficiency of service
on their respective part and every time there was problem, the given oven was
attended to and relief/repair/attendance, as was possible, was done. Denying that there was any deficiency of
service/negligence at all on part of the Ops, the complaint was stated to be
frivolous and hence, dismissal of the same with cost was prayed for.
The matter was heard with filing of evidence by the
complainant, but not on part of the Ops, when the Ld. Forum below, upon hearing
of respective parties passed its judgement and order as under :-
That the o.p. no. 1 is directed to refund Rs. 8300/-
(Rupees eight thousand three hundred) only to the complainant positively within
thirty days from the date of communication of this order, failing which it will
carry interest @ 12% p.a. till full realization. Both o.p. nos. 1 and 2 are jointly and severally directed to pay
compensation of Rs. 20,000/- (Rupees twenty thousand) only to the complainant
along with litigation cost of Rs. 3000/- (Rupees three thousand) only
positively within thirty days from the date of communication of this order to
the o.ps., failing which it will carry interest @ 10% p.a. till
realization. Fees paid are correct.
Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgement
and order of the Ld. Forum below, the Ops in the Forum namely (1) Great Eastern
Appliances Pvt. Ltd. and (2) Videocon Industries Ltd., filed this Appeal when
it stated inter alia that the Complainant/Respondent No. 1 filed malfunction
reports in branch office and head office selectively resulting in mismatch of
communications. Contending that the
Appellant was diligent in attending to every report of malfunction through
appropriate agencies and even went for replacement of the given oven without any
cost, it stated that the firstly the complaint was not backed by appropriate
technical report and secondly, there was no expert evidence on the issue of
malfunctioning of the oven or on its handling and problems attendant thereto. Raising the point of respective liability as
of any unit having complaints of malfunctioning thereof or otherwise between a
dealer and a manufacturer, issue was also raised on the Ld. Forums order on
refund of Rs. 8300/- which inter alia included a component of VAT amounting to
Rs. 922.22, since realized from the complainant and deposited with the
Government as per rule and practice and the same was supposedly
non-refundable. Stating that the goods
can best be replaced in extreme circumstances but no refund of purchase amount
can be made, the Appellant contended that the impugned judgement and order was
bad and hence, be set aside with further orders as deemed fit.
The Respondent No. 1 namely Mr. Santosh Kr. Kanodia, the
complainant in the Ld. Forum below, entered appearance and argued inter alia
that while the Complainant/Respondent No. 1 filed evidence on affidavit,
neither the OP No. 1 nor the OP No. 2 namely (1) Great Eastern Appliances Pvt.
Ltd. and (2) Videocon Industries Ltd., cared to file any evidence on their part
and thus his evidence remained uncontroverted.
Stating that the Appeal was not filed in terms of Section 15 or in terms
of Rule 8(1), it was pointed out that there was no memorandum of appeal as such
and thus the petition was liable to be dismissed with cost. Reiterating the plight of
Complainant/Respondent No. 1 it was denied that the purchase price was not
refundable and accordingly the Respondent No. 1 prayed for affirmation of the
judgement and order of the Ld. Forum below and orders for its compliance.
Respondent No. 2 namely Videocon Industries Ltd., also
entered appearance and contended that the complainant could not have prayed for
refund of purchase money without alternative prayer and no order could be
passed by the Ld. Forum below without any expert technical opinion on the given
alleged defective goods. Accordingly,
the Respondent No. 2 prayed for setting aside of the impugned judgement and
order.
The matter was heard from respective sides. Following citations were relied upon by the
Appellant and Respondent No. 2.

 DISCUSSION

 

A. There is not much dispute as to the fact of the case where the
Respondent No. 1/Complainant bought on due consideration one Microwave Oven
that malfunctioned again and again and after some prodding, was required to be
replaced, which again, after a short while, did not function and thus the complaint
case. We have carefully gone through
the evidence of the Complainant/Respondent No. 1, which remain uncontroverted
by the two Ops, namely the Appellant (M/s. Great Eastern Appliances Pvt. Ltd.)
and Respondent No. 2 (M/s. Videocon Industries Ltd.). We are in full agreement with the findings of the Ld. Forum below
and find that the award of the refund amount accepted towards consideration of
the given Microwave Oven at Rs. 8300/- was perfectly in order. The Appellants argument that the said
amount included an amount of Rs. 922.22 being VAT and also that there is no
provision for refund of price paid but defective goods could be replaced, do
not hold water. The VAT payment was a
corollary and consequence to the sale of the given product and the product
having being found altogether malfunctional and again so even after
replacement, thus the only option left with the Respondent No. 1/Complainant
was to go for a new Microwave Oven, in the event he decided so and then he
would be required, under provisions, to pay VAT again. The other issue raised by the Appellant that
there could not be refund of price but replacement only also has no application
here as the Respondent No. 1/Complainant cannot be subjected to unlimited
replacements of Microwave Ovens and consequential harassment when replacement
has been found to be malfunctional by nature and do not operate at times of
use. Accordingly, we find that the
order of the Ld. Forum below towards refund of purchase price being 8300/- is
perfectly in order.
B. As for the question of compensation and litigation cost awarded
on Appellant/OP No. 1 and Respondent No. 2/OP No. 2, we find the given amounts
as reasonable, fair and quite in proportion to the deficiency of
service/negligence suffered by the Respondent No. 1/Complainant. In that view, the award of compensation of
Rs. 20,000/- and litigation cost of Rs. 3000/- payable by the Appellant &
Respondent No. 2 (OP Nos. 1 & 2 in the Forum below) are also found to be in
order. In such regard, the citations
relied upon by the Appellant have been gone through but have been found to have
no application in the facts and circumstances of this case.
C. In above view, the impugned judgement and order of the Ld.
Forum below is liable to be affirmed and the Appeal is also liable to be
dismissed on contest with cost of Rs. 1,000/- to the paid by the Appellant to
the Respondent No. 1/Complainant.
O R D E R

 

 The Appeal stands dismissed on contest with cost of Rs.
1,000/- (Rupees one thousand only) to be paid by the Appellant to the
Respondent No. 1/Complainant and the impugned judgement stands affirmed. The Appellant and Respondent No. 2 are
directed to pay the decretal dues along with the cost imposed by us to the
Respondent No. 1/Complainant within one (1) month from the date of receipt of
this judgement, failing which the same will accrue interest @ 10% (ten per
cent) per annum for the period of default.
